12: The first identity follows by induction from hv=ell v. For the second, the base i=0 is xyv=yxv+hv=ell v. If xy^i v=i(ell−i+1)y^(i−1)v, then
13:   xy^(i+1)v=y(xy^i v)+hy^i v
14:             =[i(ell−i+1)+(ell−2i)]y^i v
15:             =(i+1)(ell−i)y^i v.
16: Thus this induction does not use any termination assertion.
17: 
18: For 0≤i≤ell, applying x repeatedly gives
19:   x^i y^i v=[product_(r=1,...,i) r(ell−r+1)]v.
20: Every factor is a positive integer if i>0 and hence is nonzero in C; for i=0 the product is 1. Since v≠0, y^i v≠0. Define e_i=y^i v/i!, which is also nonzero. The eigenvalues a_i=ell−2i are pairwise distinct in C: equality would imply 2(i−j)=0 in characteristic zero and hence i=j.
21: 
22: To prove independence, take a relation sum_i z_i e_i=0 and fix j. Apply the composition product_(k≠j)(h−a_k Id). Each e_i with i≠j is killed by the factor k=i. The surviving term is
23:   z_j [product_(k≠j)(a_j−a_k)] e_j=0.
24: Every scalar factor and e_j is nonzero, so z_j=0. This works for every j and includes the singleton index set. By B001 the ell+1 vectors span V of dimension ell+1, and independence together with spanning defines a basis.
25: 
26: The first recurrence also makes z=y^(ell+1)v an h-eigenvector with eigenvalue a=−ell−2 (the vector z is permitted to be zero). Expand z in this basis using B006. Applying h−a Id gives
27:   sum_i z_i(a_i−a)e_i=0.
28: For i≤ell, a_i−a=2(ell+1−i)≠0 in C. Independence gives every z_i=0, so z=0. All higher lowering powers vanish as well. Dividing the recurrences by i!, and using (i+1)!=(i+1)i!, now gives exactly
29:   xe_0=0; xe_i=(ell−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤ell;
30:   ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<ell; ye_ell=0;
31:   he_i=(ell−2i)e_i.
32: For r≤i, iterating x gives the coefficient product_(s=1,...,r)(ell−i+s) on e_(i−r). Division by r! gives choose(ell−i+r,r), by B004 with n=ell−i+r and j=r and cancellation of the nonzero factorial (ell−i)!. If r>i, the lowering in index reaches e_0 and is then killed by x. For i+r≤ell, iterating y gives (i+r)!/i! on e_(i+r); division by r! gives choose(i+r,r) by B004. If i+r>ell, the string reaches e_ell and is killed by y. These are precisely the divided-power formulas for all r, including r=0. This proves B101 from B001, B004, and B006.
33: 
34: B102: integral scaled matrix units on the arbitrary lattice.
35:

7: The complete [neutral JSON example](../templates/quantified-implication-example.md)
8: shows an arbitrary binder, a local antecedent, its discharge and the full
9: quantified output. Follow this accounting rather than silently granting a
10: property in a local object's type.
11: 
12: ## Implication and contradiction
13: 
14: To prove `X -> Y`, introduce X inside one argument, derive Y from the declared
15: inputs, then discharge X into the antecedent. Output `X -> Y`, not Y. To use Y
16: unconditionally later, supply an actually proved X and apply implication
17: elimination. A local X and a proved X are not the same proof object.
18: 
19: To prove `not X`, derive false under local X and discharge X by negation
20: introduction. To prove P by classical contradiction, first produce the complete
21: theorem `not P -> false` (equivalently `not not P`), then apply the fixed
22: classical rule. A single R may combine the operations if every local assumption
23: is accounted for. No classical double-negation elimination under an
24: intuitionistic-only policy.
25: 
26: Example graph: N1 `(not P -> Q)`, N2 `not Q`, R1 outputs N3
27: `(not P -> false)`, R2 outputs P. The argument of R1 locally assumes not P,
28: applies N1 and N2, and closes that assumption. No `not P` root is added.
29: The fallacy “assume P, obtain P, discharge and output P” fails: its valid output
30: would be `P -> P`.
31: 
32: ## Cases
33: 
34: From an already proved `A or B or C`, obtain a common target Q by complete
35: conditional lemmas `A -> Q`, `B -> Q`, `C -> Q`, then disjunction elimination.
36: Alternatively prove `not A`, `not B` and conclude C using the original
37: disjunction. Eliminating A/B without a proved exhaustive disjunction cannot
38: establish C. A branch producing false can produce the common target by false
39: elimination; it does not make false an unconditional source proposition.
40: 
41: Proof bodies may contain all branches locally instead of exporting every
42: branch lemma. Check coverage, identical target/ambient context, and the absence
43: of sibling-branch fact/witness leakage. Introduce/discharge each branch-local
44: assumption in its actual scope.
45: 
46: ## Quantifiers, witnesses, and induction
47: 
48: For universal introduction use an arbitrary variable, then close its binder.
49: It must not occur free in an undischarged extra assumption. If the intended
50: theorem has a premise H(x), retain it in the quantified implication.
51: 
52: For existential elimination start from a proved existence statement, choose a
53: fresh local witness with exactly its stated properties, and prove a conclusion
54: independent of that witness's private identity. A witness depending on n does
55: not yield one witness valid for every n. Do not turn a local witness into a
56: globally available constant without a legitimate, recorded construction.
57: 
58: For natural-number induction prove the base and the complete step
59: `forall n, Q(n) -> Q(n+1)` and use induction to conclude `forall n, Q(n)`.
60: The induction hypothesis is local to the step; there is no circular graph edge.
61: If the step invokes the hypothesis at a transformed point s, include
62: `forall s` in the induction invariant. Well-founded induction needs the exact
63: well-founded relation/decrease justification; the word “induct” is not enough.
64: 
65: ## Local notation
66: 
67: Global symbols are reserved. Local binders can repeat across separate nodes
68: or separate binding scopes in a node, but cannot shadow a global symbol.
69: `sum_{k=1}^N` binds k only in that expression. Source theorem dummy variables
70: are alpha-renamed locally, not registered as a new global object each time.
71: Freshness, witness dependencies, constant uniformity, and binder scope are
72: mathematical audit obligations; a list of names does not verify the formula.
73: In v2, local declarations identify introduction kind/basis and inclusive S
74: start/end positions. An input-bound name needs instantiation; a witness needs
75: an actual existence premise. Local F facts record their complete statement,
76: statement-local binders, used objects and remaining assumptions. Neither a
77: fact nor a chosen witness may escape its scope. The checker accounts for
78: declared scopes; Audit A must also inspect the actual quantifier reasoning."}

{"id": "problem.md", "total_lines": 190, "start": 1, "end": 117, "start_column": 0, "end_column": 0, "requested_end": 117, "has_more": true, "next_start": 118, "next_column": 0, "next_end": 190, "text": "1: # Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero
46: 
47: Put \(n=\lambda+1\) and \(e_i=y^iv/i!\) for \(0\leq i\leq\lambda\).
48: The commutator identities give, by induction,
49: 
50: \[
51: hy^iv=(\lambda-2i)y^iv,\qquad
52: xy^iv=i(\lambda-i+1)y^{i-1}v\quad(i\geq1).
53: \]
54: 
55: For \(i\leq\lambda\), applying \(x^i\) to \(y^iv\) gives
56: \(i!\lambda(\lambda-1)\cdots(\lambda-i+1)v\ne0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
57: At \(i=0\) the empty product is one. Thus every \(e_i\ne0\).
58: Their \(h\)-eigenvalues \(\lambda-2i\) are distinct over \(\mathbb C\),
59: so they are linearly independent: applying
60: \(\prod_{k\ne j}(h-(\lambda-2k)\mathrm{Id})\) to a relation isolates
61: its \(j\)-th coefficient with a nonzero multiplier.
62: There are \(n\) vectors, the dimension of \(V(\lambda)\), hence they
63: form a basis. Also \(y^{\lambda+1}v=0\), since otherwise it would be
64: an eigenvector of eigenvalue \(-\lambda-2\), absent from this basis.
65: All higher lowering powers vanish as well.
66: 
67: The operator matrices are therefore
68: 
69: \[
70: xe_0=0,\quad xe_i=(\lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}\ (i\geq1),\qquad
71: ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1}\ (i<\lambda),\quad ye_\lambda=0,
72: \quad he_i=(\lambda-2i)e_i.
73: \]
74: 
75: Iteration gives the integral divided-power matrices
76: 
77: \[
78: X_re_i=\binom{\lambda-i+r}{r}e_{i-r}\quad(0\leq r\leq i),
79: \qquad
80: Y_re_i=\binom{i+r}{r}e_{i+r}\quad(i+r\leq\lambda).       \tag{1}
81: \]
82: 
83: The respective expressions are zero when \(r>i\) or
84: \(i+r>\lambda\), by termination of the strings just proved.
85: 
86: ### 2. Matrix units preserve the localized arbitrary lattice
87: 
88: Let \(R=\mathbb Z_{(p)}=\{a/b\in\mathbb Q:p\nmid b\}\), and regard
89: \(M_R=R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}M\) as a submodule of \(V(\lambda)\).
90: The embedding is injective because an integer basis of \(M\) is
91: complex-linearly independent. The module \(M_R\) is free of rank \(n\)
92: over \(R\) and is preserved by all \(X_r,Y_r\), by admissibility.
93: 
94: Define \(E_{ij}\) to send \(e_j\) to \(e_i\) and all other basis
95: vectors to zero. Formula (1) gives
96: 
97: \[
98: P:=Y_\lambda X_\lambda=E_{\lambda\lambda},\qquad
99: X_{\lambda-i}P=E_{i\lambda},\qquad
100: P Y_{\lambda-j}=\binom\lambda j E_{\lambda j}.
101: \]
102: 
103: For the last identity, an input index below \(j\) is sent below
104: \(e_\lambda\) and killed by \(P\); an index above \(j\) is sent past
105: the end of the lowering string. On \(e_j\) the coefficient is precisely
106: \(\binom\lambda j\). Since \(\lambda<p\), none of
107: \(\lambda!\), \(j!\), \((\lambda-j)!\) is divisible by \(p\), so
108: \(\binom\lambda j\) is a unit in \(R\). Consequently
109: 
110: \[
111: E_{ij}=\left(\binom\lambda j\right)^{-1}
112:        X_{\lambda-i}P Y_{\lambda-j}.                 \tag{2}
113: \]
114: 
115: Every matrix unit preserves \(M_R\). No assertion about distinct
116: weights modulo \(p\) has been used.
117: "}

namespace YuiBasisObjects

noncomputable def dividedPower {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r

def Stable {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    (W : Submodule K V) (f : Module.End K V) : Prop :=
  ∀ w, w ∈ W → f w ∈ W

structure AdmissibleLattice (n : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (x y : Module.End ℂ V) where
  carrier : Submodule ℤ V
  zBasis : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℤ carrier
  cBasis : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℂ V
  coe_basis : ∀ i, (zBasis i : V) = cBasis i
  stableX : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : V), m ∈ carrier → dividedPower x r m ∈ carrier
  stableY : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : V), m ∈ carrier → dividedPower y r m ∈ carrier

end YuiBasisObjects
"}

target_review.notes: Compared the complete problem (including its original proof) with target-selection, proof-context, spec and P. The ambient parameters carry only their stated structures; all original substantive conditions occur in H001–H007, whose graph statements equal the specification. Prime p, arbitrary characteristic-p field K, integer 0≤lambda<p, dimension lambda+1, the exact Chevalley normalization and highest-weight data, and arbitrary U_Z-stable admissible M are preserved. P includes both nonzeroness and every invariant K-subspace being zero or whole, using the original M⊗K and formal Chevalley algebra, including lambda=0 and p=2. No constant dependency is changed. The authorized B101/B102/B104/B103/B105/B106 route corresponds to N001/N002/N003/N004/N005/P. All six replacement entries were compared: localization, rational coordinate rank and valuation/principal-ideal claims are eliminated, while integral operator identities, tensor swap and abstract matrix-unit dimension reasoning are internal derivations. The common-basis reindexing uses B007/M008–M009 rather than imposing a special lattice. H004 remains in full although its complex-irreducibility component is not needed beyond the retained dimension/highest-weight data. This is target and route fidelity, not approval of unreviewed R bodies.

D001.notes: Int.toNat is a total natural-valued construction from the integer parameter. Equality lambda=(ell:Z) is exported by N001, rather than assumed in this definition; H003 retains nonnegativity.

D002.notes: n=ell+1 defines a positive finite index length. Fin(n) gives exactly 0≤i≤ell; integer subtraction in weight formulas is explicitly distinguished from natural index subtraction.

D003.notes: The divided power is defined over C for every natural r, including r=0. Factorials have nonzero complex images; this introduces neither a characteristic-p division nor a stability assumption.

D004.notes: The analogous lowering divided powers are defined for every natural r over C, with the usual zeroth power. Their lattice preservation is separately guarded by H007.

D005.notes: U_Z is the original generated integer subalgebra of the enveloping algebra; its represented generators are distinguished from the abstract algebra. This preserves precisely the original admissibility condition.

D006.notes: This is the original tensor product M⊗_Z K and its second-factor K-action. It exists for the ambient Z-module M without freeness or nonzeroness; neither property is assumed here.

D007.notes: The auxiliary tensor product reverses the factors and uses the first-factor K-action. It is not silently identified with V_K: S and its inverse are defined separately and their properties are exported by N003.

D008.notes: Stable is the universally quantified preservation predicate for a linear subspace and an endomorphism over the same arbitrary field. All dummy objects are locally bound.

D009.notes: The vectors e_i are explicitly defined from v,y and complex factorial inverses on Fin(n). This definition grants no basis property, integrality, or membership in M; N001 supplies the basis theorem.

D010.notes: The restriction X_r|M exists because H007 says every represented divided-power generator preserves M. Its inherited Z-linearity gives End_Z(M); the H007 guard is retained.

D011.notes: The lowering restriction is likewise well-defined and Z-linear under the explicit H007 admissibility guard, without assuming individual e_i belong to M.

D012.notes: X_M(1) is exactly the restriction of x because 1!=1. The inherited H007 guard is explicit.

D013.notes: Y_M(1) is exactly the restriction of y because 1!=1. The inherited H007 guard is explicit.

D014.notes: The commutator of two Z-endomorphisms is a well-defined Z-endomorphism. Equality to the restriction of h is reserved for N002 using H005; no preservation of h is smuggled into the definition.

D015.notes: The binomial coefficient is natural-valued on j≤ell supplied by Fin(ell+1). Its nonzero reduction is not assumed; it is an N004 conclusion.

D016.notes: The composition of restricted divided powers defines an integral endomorphism under H007. No projection or matrix-unit property is granted here.

D017.notes: All factors are integral endomorphisms under H007. For i,j∈Fin(ell+1), ell−i and ell−j are nonnegative natural indices. The order of composition agrees with the authorized basis route.

D018.notes: The finite product of the c_j is a defined natural number. No invertibility, divisibility, or nonzero property is assumed.

D019.notes: The finite product omitting j is well-defined, with empty product 1, covering ell=0. The product identity with c_j is subsequently exported by N002.

D020.notes: The rule (a,m)↦a⊗f(m) is additive and Z-balanced since f is Z-linear, hence induces an additive tensor map; it commutes with K-scaling on the first factor. Ring-homomorphism laws are expressly left to N003/E001.

D021.notes: Tensor swapping is additive and Z-balanced: (zm)⊗a and m⊗(za) map to equal balanced tensors. Thus the additive map exists without any basis choice; K-linearity and invertibility are separate N003 conclusions.

D022.notes: The reversed balanced tensor formula similarly defines an additive map. Its name does not assume the inverse laws; those are in N003.

D023.notes: This is the canonical integer homomorphism into the field, which exists independently of its characteristic. Sum/product/one preservation belongs to that canonical construction; its kernel and nonzero factorial images are not assumed.

D024.notes: Field inverse is explicitly total, so this definition is meaningful even before proving red(c_j)≠0. Cancellation and the normalized matrix-unit relations are N004 obligations; H007 guards A_ij.

D025.notes: The rule (m,a)↦f(m)⊗a is additive and Z-balanced, and commutes with K-scaling on the second factor. It therefore defines exactly the original induced lattice operator for any integral endomorphism.

D026.notes: The formal rank-three Chevalley Z-module is distinguished from its possibly nonfaithful represented image, preserving the lambda=0 case. The displayed alternating bilinear bracket is consistent: Jacobi on the distinct basis triple is 0+2h−2h=0, and repeated-generator cases cancel.

D027.notes: Scalar extension of that formal integral Lie algebra defines the original Chevalley L_K, including characteristic 2. The assigned generators initially give a K-linear map; bracket preservation is deferred to proof. H007 and N002 are explicit guards and are direct inputs to the sole consumer R006.
